keyQuestions.text: KQ1 [architecture] How does nodeterm drive one agent core over three carriers (Electron preload, browser WebSocket, E2EE relay tunnel) behind a single RpcClient/FrameTransport contract, and what is the exact transport interface, frame discrimination, in-flight failure, and RPC envelope shape?

KQ2 [security] What is the exact layered security envelope of nodeterm's untrusted-relay E2EE design (NaCl box, HKDF per-session keys, seq anti-replay, role check, SAS mutual approval, approval-from-ciphertext-only rule), and which specific attack does each layer defeat?

KQ3 [logic] How does reduceEntry reduce raw agent hook events into working/waiting/blocked/done status without race-condition false flips (DONE_HOLDOFF, stale-working sweeper, interrupt inference, awaitingInput hold, idle-rescue, newTurn gating, transient-vs-persisted fields)?

KQ4 [logic] How does nodeterm normalize heterogeneous agent transcript/hook formats into one universal event shape (NormalizedAgentEvent, per-agent normalizers), and how does it tail live transcripts including subagent fan-out and context-window fill?

KQ5 [ease-of-use] How does hook-reply Approve/Deny deliver deterministic approvals without keystroke injection (per-decision answer files, pendingId generation and path-traversal validation, stale sweeping, fail-open timeout, askKind distinction, re-read-before-send)?

KQ6 [ux] What data contract (MirrorFile/MirrorInbox, InboxEvent, InboxNodeNow) powers the mobile companion screen, and what are its event production, title/dedup, resolve/archive, live-card, and quick-approve rules?

KQ7 [ux] How does nodeterm keep remote sessions usable across drops (connected/connecting/offline model, reconnect-in-place, ready()-can-hang fix, carrier-close in-flight failure, WS heartbeat/reap, backpressure and frame-size caps)?

KQ8 [ease-of-use] How does push-notification decisioning decide when to ping the phone (batch window, per-node throttle, presence-aware hold queue, grant model, three-surface degrade, deliver-on-idle with flush-time re-validation)?

keyFindings.text: F-1 — The carrier seam is a four-method interface with exactly two implementations
F-2 — Frame discrimination: string = JSON RPC frame, Uint8Array = binary pty-data
F-3 — Carrier close fails every in-flight request BEFORE overlay hooks, with a coded error
F-4 — One api surface rebuilt over either carrier by reusing the same builders
F-5 — RPC envelope: five `t`-discriminated shapes, incrementing-id correlation, out-of-band `undef`
F-6 — Early-event replay buffer closes the open-vs-subscribe race
F-7 — The third surface: a stub api whose degrades are typed, deliberate, and compiler-enforced
F-1 — Additive inbox block rides the existing v1 mirror file; no new transport
F-2 — InboxEvent / InboxNodeNow / MirrorInbox shapes with hard caps
F-3 — Event production: stash-priority classification, not raw state mapping
F-4 — Dedup is TITLE-based and bounded, and survives restarts
F-5 — Resolve/archive/live-card lifecycle: host owns resolution, phone owns reading
F-6 — Quick-approve: re-read-before-send; SSH slices keep a filtered inbox
F-1 — Held-hook + answer-file contract: the reply channel is a file on the host the agent runs on

keyFindings.text: F-1 — Three-state session status model mutated in place
F-2 — Involuntary drop keeps the entry and binding; user close does not
F-3 — ready()-can-hang trap fixed by racing approval against real close signal plus timeout backstop
F-4 — Offline tab is a connection bookmark: grey out, click-to-reconnect, deferred stale-session disposal
F-5 — Carrier close fails in-flight requests and shows the reconnect overlay (transport contract)
F-6 — WS heartbeat/reap: ping every 30 s, one missed round terminates, sized for proxy idle timeouts
F-7 — 8 MiB frame cap rejects oversized frames pre-dispatch as shared-process DoS guard
F-01 — One actionable-event seam feeds BOTH the inbox and the push service
F-02 — Batch window coalesces close-together events; hard cap of 10 events per POST; the gate is re-checked at flush time
F-03 — Per-node 5-second throttle, charged only when an event is accepted
F-04 — Presence-aware hold queue: hold alerts while the user is at the desktop, flush the still-unresolved ones on the present→away edge
F-05 — Grant model: SSH possession IS the authorization — a capability file the phone drops, zero open ports, self-healing dead-mark
F-06 — Remote grant sweep + per-device dedupe; targeting is a UNION, and the residual double-push is documented as the cheap side of the tradeoff
F-07 — Deliberate three-surface degrade: the service ships everywhere but only the surface with prerequisites constructs it
F-08 — Delivery-queue deliver-on-idle: flush-time re-validation is the load-bearing property, and no outcome is ever silent
F-09 — The live-update stream: state edges post fast, activity ticks coalesce, and a parked tick can never contradict an end edge
F-01 — DONE_HOLDOFF: a 3 s parallel-hook guard duplicated on both sides of the seam
F-02 — Stale-working sweeper: ONE constant, ONE decider, one synthetic end edge
F-03 — Interrupt inference: settle window + unchanged freshness baseline
F-04 — awaitingInput hold: a needs-you that survives its own turn-end done
F-05 — Idle-rescue: may only move a still-working node, and remembers which kind of done it is
F-06 — newTurn gating: one explicit turn-start flag gates resurrection, fan-out reset, and guard clearing
F-07 — Transient vs persisted: persist identity, never live state or clocks; label restored evidence
F-01 — One universal event shape; per-agent normalizers absorb every dialect
F-02 — Fixtures confirm how heterogeneous the raw formats are
F-03 — Transcript reader: bounded tails, traversal-proof ids, account-scoped caching
F-04 — Transcript index: pure helpers, mtime-incremental refresh, parser-consistent with the chat view
F-05 — Subagent tail: meta-correlated fan-out streaming with tear-safe carries
F-06 — Context tail: backward-scanned usage, per-agent parse dep owns the denominator, two free side-channel signals
F-07 — Activity strings + contextPercent: the raw-listener → mobile live-card pipeline
F-01 — NaCl box authenticated encryption with strict key validation and fail-closed decrypt
F-02 — Two-key separation: stable baseKey (identity/SAS) vs per-session HKDF traffic key
F-03 — Sealed-plaintext header `[role][seq][tag]`: all security metadata inside the box
F-04 — Role-byte-must-equal-peer check (anti-reflection)
F-05 — Strictly-increasing inbound anti-replay seq
F-06 — Handshake processed exactly once: no mid-session re-key + per-frame peer-key pin
F-07 — Out-of-band 6-digit SAS with mutual approval and pin-once peer keys
F-08 — Approval advances ONLY from ciphertext: the single trust choke point
F-09 — Endianness discipline traps (three different byte orders in one protocol)
F-01 — Sealed `[role][seq][tag]` header construction VERIFIED at primary lines (upgrades iteration-9 F-03)
F-02 — Receiver check chain VERIFIED: decrypt → length ≥ 9 → role == PEER_ROLE → seq strictly increasing → strip + dispatch (upgrades iteration-9 F-04/F-05)
F-03 — Handshake-frozen-after-ready VERIFIED: late control frames dropped without re-key or close (upgrades iteration-9 F-06)
F-04 — Exactly-once processing mechanics VERIFIED with new primary detail (not recorded in iteration 9)
F-05 — relay-client.ts client-half obligations now primary-cited (iteration 9 held only the host-side pin via doc)
F-06 — Relay-side timing constants anchored; reconnect backoff table is DEAD CODE (nuance/correction)

Nothing ruled out this iteration; no approach failed. One near-misreading corrected en route: the renderer sweeper and the mirror sweep are NOT one mechanism — they are two deliberate layers with different semantics (renderer blanks to Unknown for local badges; mirror commits `done` + synthetic stale end edge for phone/notch surfaces). Recorded as F-02 evidence, not a dead end.

**framing.ts as a live KQ2 security layer.** Read in full per the focus list; it is the LEGACY opcode dialect the Stage-4 migration deletes (`OP.*` codes, snapshot flow) [SOURCE: specs/context/nodeterm-main/docs/ios-protocol-migration.md:471-489, 636]. Its residual relevance is the little-endian 16-byte header pattern (F-09) and the shared backpressure constant `MAX_BINARY_BUFFERED_AMOUNT` (KQ7 territory) — not security enforcement. Not retried as a security source.
**relay-client.ts / relay-socket.ts direct reads this iteration.** Deferred under the 12-call budget in favor of the four core security files + the protocol doc; see Edge Cases.

Re-verifying `src/server/ws.ts` heartbeat/reap constants: already primary-cited in iteration 4; relay-socket.ts carries only the relay-side analog (`KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_MS = 25_000` encrypted keepalive), so a ws.ts reread would add nothing this iteration.
Treating `RECONNECT_DELAYS_MS`/`scheduleReconnect` as a live auto-reconnect mechanism: defined but never invoked; reconnection is caller-owned via fresh-token mint (see F-06).
